note: Labels for the office-reply rule (src/office_rule.js). Everything here is fictional. The labels were written by the author of the rule, by hand, before the rule was run on these messages for the first time, so they show whether the rule does what its author intends and not how often real office messages fit it. The block called measured was added after the runs and is checked by cli/check_office.js.
order_note: A message can carry more than one kind. The label is the kind that comes first in this fixed order, which is also the order the rule uses: process_change, cannot_find, cancellation_processed, date_time_change, deadline, ack_named, link_or_number, ack_no_name. A message with none of these, or with a request or a problem that none of these explains, is for_person.
cells_note: cells lists the sheet cells a careful coordinator would fill or change from this one message, among the cells the rule covers: Hearings K, BD, AW, N, BA, BH, AF, AV, BN, BJ, D, E, I, J, H, L, Y and Offices M. A message for a person has none, because the rule proposes nothing for it.
round16_note: On 20 Nov 2026 (round 16) the gate sheet gained cells, and the labels were extended by one fixed rule, not message by message: every label of the kind process_change gained "Offices AS" and "Offices AT" (3 labels), and every label of the kind cannot_find gained "Hearings AA", "Hearings CP" and "Hearings CQ" (3 labels). No kind was changed and no other cell was added or removed.
round18_note: On 21 Nov 2026 (round 18) the gate sheet gained Hearings DR (the date a moved hearing had before) and the kit's rule became "clear K as well as J and H, and keep the old link in a note". The labels were extended by one fixed rule, not message by message: every label of the kind date_time_change that holds "Hearings D" (a new date in writing) gained "Hearings DR" and "Hearings K" (2 labels: messages 17 and 47). No kind was changed and no other cell was added or removed.

unseen_note: The 30 unseen messages in data/heldout.json are all office messages about new situations, written by a separate writer for the readers. The author of the rule labelled them here by hand after the rule was frozen and before the rule was run on them, and the rule was not changed afterwards. One of them, H031, was seen by the author before the rule was written, so the counts are also given without it. Here cells may name a cell the rule does not cover (Hearings O, the proof that something owed was processed): the rule cannot be right on the cells of such a message.

measured.note: Measured on 19 Nov 2026 by running node cli/office.js --measure. cli/check_office.js fails if a run no longer gives these counts. Right means the kind equals the label. Cells right means the rule proposes exactly the label's set of cells.

packet_first_run.note: All three failed for one reason: the pattern for statements that need nothing typed did not match a sentence that starts with a capital, such as "No changes." The pattern was made to ignore capitals. Nothing was added for a single message.

measured.frozen_note: The rule was frozen before the unseen messages were labelled and run. Afterwards only the wording of the reason sentence was changed; kind, hold and proposals of the shipped rule were compared with the frozen copy on all 72 packet messages and all 30 unseen ones, with and without context (204 comparisons, 0 differ). On 20 Nov 2026 (round 15d) two things were changed in the rule, neither from the unseen results: the HOLD sentence was reworded (the recorded route waits for a person; notices go by both routes until the office confirms in writing), and an office's arrival instruction is now proposed for Hearings CI as minutes and no longer for Hearings AV (sheet rule S15). Compared with the copy before the change on the same 204 comparisons, 2 differ, both on packet message 40, and 0 of the 60 on the unseen messages.
measured.round16_note: On 20 Nov 2026 (round 16) the rule was changed again, not from the unseen results but because the gate sheet gained cells: the HOLD sentence became the sheet's block sentence (no notice goes to the office until a person approves the change), a process change now also proposes Offices AS and AT, and a notice the office cannot find now also proposes Hearings CP, CQ and AA, with a reworded task in Hearings Y. Compared with the copy before the change on the same 204 comparisons (72 packet messages and 30 unseen ones, with and without context): kind differs in 0, hold and forPerson differ in 0, and the proposals differ in 10, on packet messages 16, 22 and 24 and on unseen messages H036 and H057, every one of them only by the new cells and the reworded Y. Through the inbox connector the office rule therefore proposes 24 lines on the unseen messages (20 before): the 4 new ones are Offices AS and AT for H036 and H057.

simulation.note: The prepared answers were written by the author of the rule, so this shows the handling of each kind and is not a measure of accuracy.

measured.unseen_wrong_proposals_note: On three unseen messages the rule proposed a cell that a person should not fill. H047: it also proposed Hearings L, because "We have now processed the withdrawal ... and the file was closed" matched the pattern for a receipt of case files. H059: it read "Requests to change this date must be made in writing no later than June 14" as a deadline and proposed Hearings AW and BH. H038: it read "A staffing notice reached us ... and has been processed" as an acknowledgment without a name, missed "Our Monday list now shows Owen Tarris" and "Nothing has been filed for 14 Willow Lane", and proposed only Hearings Y. The rule was not changed after this run, so these three defects are still in it.
